explanation: In Italy, patting someone on the head is considered patronizing or disrespectful, as the head is viewed as a personal and inviolable space. This gesture is typically reserved for children or pets, and doing it to an adult at a social gathering can be seen as condescending. Italians value personal boundaries and physical contact is generally limited to handshakes, cheek kisses, or friendly shoulder touches among acquaintances.
local_tip: Instead of patting the head, offer a firm handshake or a light touch on the arm to show friendliness.
regional_note: In southern Italy, where physical contact is more common among friends, head patting is still avoided as it carries the same negative connotation.

also_check.note: The head is considered the most sacred body part in Thai culture, and touching it is a major taboo.
Patting the head of an adult is generally seen as disrespectful, though it may be acceptable for close family or children.
In casual settings, a light pat on the head can be a friendly gesture, though it may still be seen as overly familiar by some.
